statements.status_notes: Restricted (non-root) bind mounts took the source path from fstab but did not pin it before the privileged mount, so a local user able to replace the source or a writable ancestor could redirect the SUID mount to another host directory, and X-mount.owner, X-mount.group or X-mount.mode then changed that directory's ownership or mode as root. Upstream fixed it in util-linux 2.41.6 (commits https://github.com/util-linux/util-linux/commit/9fcb98bf08d9119d07ba3a3c709b1a85e4a1bbcb and https://github.com/util-linux/util-linux/commit/b21f4cee55f723b045920dad5ce48a659d34cac8) and 2.42.3 (commits https://github.com/util-linux/util-linux/commit/9a8d0d60c55d3a55f89f6f75a17bae31bc5ee1c6 and https://github.com/util-linux/util-linux/commit/6051830a27a852fed92ebd8493e57aa3d5d9cf18); see https://github.com/util-linux/util-linux/security/advisories/GHSA-rh77-686x-2f2m and https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-78410. Checked the libmount library in every published build of the DHI Alpine 3.23 util-linux packages (2.41.2-r0, 2.41.4-r0, 2.41.6-r0 and 2.41.6-r1) on x86_64 and aarch64. These packages are built from the upstream release tarball for their version, with Alpine's packaging patches, and each libmount reports that upstream version. 2.41.2-r0 and 2.41.4-r0 (util-linux 2.41.2 and 2.41.4) are affected; 2.41.6-r0 and 2.41.6-r1 (util-linux 2.41.6) include the fix. The range ends at 2.41.6-r0.
